findings.description: PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-01 missed. Document shows LMIA issue/expiry 2024-02-01/2024-08-01 (expired before 2025-02-01 offer) and 'Expired Work Permit (No Legal Authorization)'; narrative explicitly states LMIA expired Aug 1, 2024 and loss of work authorization. Worker emitted only a generic requirements statement and flagged nothing.

PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-01 missed (scanned sibling). Identical expired-LMIA / expired work permit defect present and explicitly narrated; worker returned only generic letter requirements with no defect detection.

PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-02 missed. Employment_type 'Part-Time, Temporary Seasonal', 20 hrs/week, 6-month contract (2025-03-01 to 2025-09-01) fails the continuous/full-time/non-seasonal/1-year post-PR test. Worker did not flag; prose restated generic requirements only.

PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-02 missed (scanned sibling). Part-time/seasonal 20 hrs/week 6-month term present; worker only recited the full completeness-check requirement without comparing it against the document's disqualifying terms.

PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-03 missed. NOC 65102 / TEER 5 (Store Shelf Stocker) is ineligible and conflicts with the LMIA's skilled Software Developer (NOC 21232, TEER 1); narrative states the conflict outright. Worker flagged nothing.
PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-03 missed (scanned sibling). TEER 5 duties mismatched to LMIA TEER 1 with explicit conflict narrative; worker's prose only paraphrased generic letter requirements.
PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-04 missed. Wage_rate 25.00 CAD/hr is below the 46.00 prevailing rate and below the 48.50 LMIA-approved rate; narrative states both. Worker did not detect the wage defect.
PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-04 missed (scanned sibling). Offered wage 25.00 below prevailing/LMIA rate explicitly narrated; worker returned generic requirements with no wage comparison.
Claim appends 'associated LMIA details' to the letter-content requirement, which is not part of the cited completeness-check letter requirements and exceeds the provided quote.

Correctly clean (meets_requirements), but the worker never affirmatively verified LMIA validity, full-time/continuous terms, NOC/TEER-LMIA alignment, or wage-vs-prevailing; a 'pass' by omission rather than by evaluation.

patch_recommendations.suggested_patch: Add a mandatory validation checklist the agent must evaluate against the document fields and emit as pass/defect claims: (1) LMIA validity — lmia_expiry_date must be after job_offer_date/application and work_permit_status must show valid authorization (flag PFL-WRITTEN-LMIA-01 on expiry/expired permit); (2) Employment terms — employment_type continuous, non-seasonal, full-time hours_per_week >= 30, and job_duration >= 1 year post-PR (flag PFL-02 on part-time/seasonal/short-term); (3) NOC alignment — teer_category must be 0/1/2/3 and job_title/duties must match the LMIA occupation (flag PFL-03 on TEER 4/5 or duty conflict); (4) Wage — wage_rate >= prevailing_wage_rate and >= lmia_wage_offered (flag PFL-04 when below). Require the agent to cite the Narrative Statements when they self-declare a conflict.

Direct workers that a static requirements question is only the rubric, not the deliverable: they must review the attached document field-by-field against that rubric and output defect findings (with expected_verdict-style meets/defective reasoning) rather than merely restating what a compliant letter should contain. A report that recites generic requirements without comparing them to the document's actual values is incomplete.

rationale: All 10 Gemini-3.6-flash reports treated the prompt as a literal static-knowledge question and returned only a generic restatement of the IRCC completeness-check letter requirement, never comparing it to the attached document. Consequently every one of the 8 defective cases (expired LMIA x2, part-time/seasonal x2, TEER-5/NOC-conflict x2, sub-prevailing wage x2) received defect_recall 0.0 despite the defects being explicit in structured fields and even stated verbatim in the Narrative Statements. The 2 genuinely clean cases score 1.0 on recall only because there was nothing to detect, not because the worker verified compliance. Grounding is otherwise acceptable (no invented document facts; PII fully absent from claims/prose), citations resolve to a consistent PDI corpus anchor, and there is no ground-truth leakage — but the systemic absence of document-level defect detection is the dominant, critical failure.
